To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the myeloperoxidase enzyme, in the presence of H2O2 and Br-, generates singlet molecular oxygen in a quantum efficiency comparable with that of standard chemical reactions of singlet molecular oxygen formation.

myeloperoxidase, in micromolar concentration reacting with half-m millimolar stock solution of H2O2, generates singlet molecular oxygen in 50% deuterium oxide (pH + pH = 4.6) with a quantum yield of 0.2.

the near infrared electronic emission at 1268 +/- 5 nm of singlet molecular oxygen delta is detected directly by a new ultrasensitive IR equipment in the reaction of myeloperoxidase with hydrogen peroxide.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and use of novel ultrasensitive infrared (IR) spectrophotometer for detection of near IR emission from singlet molecular oxygen delta O2 (1Delta g) at 1268nm.
the direct detection of singlet delta molecular emission by MPO at pH + pD =4.5.
the detection of the singlet molecular oxygen emission at 1268 nanometers by a new IR spectrofluorometer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MPO X H2O 2 reaction is an efficient source of singlet delta molecular dioxygen, and that this reaction may contribute to the biological activity of MPO.
myeloperoxidase is an efficient singlet molecular oxygen generator, and the reaction mechanism is most likely to be via the perhydroxyl radical intermediate, as previously suggested by us.
the MPO singlet oxygen generation is a very efficient process in the MPO X peroxide system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MPO X O2- X H2 O2 reaction in the presence of Br- generates singlet molecular oxygen with a quantum yield of approximately 0.1 at 298 K.
the MPO X H2O X Br- X BrO- X H2OXO X O2 X O2 X BrO- reaction sequence in the presence of peroxide and bromide is a major singlet delta molecular O2 source in the neutrophilic oxidative burst.
myeloperoxidase, in addition to the known generation of reactive oxygen and chlorine species, is able to produce singlet delta molecular dioxygen in vivo and in vitro.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MPO-H2O2-Br- system is an effective source of singlet oxygen.
myeloperoxidase, which is a key component of neutrophils and macrophages, generates singlet molecular oxygen in a reaction with H2O2.
the MPO X H2O 2 reaction is an efficient singlet delta oxygen generating system.
